description: The flow rules waiting for data: every retrospective decides each one keep, remove or wait, citing the window's metric keys listed here (lib/window.mjs METRICS). The script inserts the values; the agent changes none. `lessons` names the lessons row that holds the rule, by its file and the start of its rule cell.

items.question: Does the handoff threshold (finish the task group, record a handoff, continue in a fresh session) prevent the cost it is meant to, and which observed proxy should trigger it? It is the first removal candidate if it is not load-bearing.

lessons.row: The handoff threshold is observable proxies

items.question: Does re-dispatching a fix loop one capability level higher when it enters round 2 end the loop sooner than it costs?

lessons.row: A fix loop entering round 2 is re-dispatched one level higher

items.question: Would a lite path for small changes save more than it risks: is the flow's overhead a large share of a small change's time and tokens?

lessons.row: The planned lite path for small fixes

items.question: Would a one-hour cache lifetime for dispatched agents save more in rewritten cache than its write premium costs?
Does stating the task's Files, Interfaces and acceptance criteria before the first edit reduce fix rounds, review findings and fixes after merge?

lessons.row: A task's text directs the implementer to state its Files, Interfaces and acceptance criteria before the first edit
